The work can be divided into three categories: problems and methods, analysis and validation, and interpretation and delivery; the following is an editorial summary. Some positions also involve sensor and acquisition system development, field collection, and technical mentoring.

Core tasks include managing and analyzing remote sensing data, fusing other geographic data, processing imagery, designing collection or analysis methods, gathering supporting data, and reporting results.

entries: Analysis and fusion｜Manage or analyze remote sensing imagery and GIS, and fuse climate and field data.｜Deliver traceable data and supporting materials.
Collection and quality｜Design collection, analysis, and display methods, build spatial databases, and monitor quality.｜Keep method and quality records.
Methods and sensors｜Research new technologies, and develop analysis algorithms, sensors, and artifact correction.｜Use experiments to state the applicable range.

Systems and implementation｜Configure and maintain acquisition systems, and guide software and hardware implementation, installation, and testing.｜Deliver technical implementation records according to the actual position.
Domain and field｜Conduct forest carbon tracking, water body or dust cloud applications, and field data collection.｜Authorized personnel check the scenario, data, and validation.
Reporting and mentoring｜Prepare documentation and reports and train technicians; new tasks include drone acquisition procedure standards.｜Actual field work or flight still follows permissions.

values: Premise｜N1—N5 are fictional pixels, not actual observations
Complete indicator recomputation, quality screening, and independent validation to-dos in 30 minutes. The NIR and RED in the premise are already comparable reflectance and need no extra scaling.
N1｜pixel P1: NIR=0.60, RED=0.20; the premise quality flag is clear.
N2｜pixel P2: NIR=0.50, RED=0.25; the premise flags it as cloud-contaminated, so the computed value cannot be used in this exercise's valid statistics.
N3｜pixel P3: NIR=0, RED=0; the denominator is zero.
N4｜the premise gives no coordinates, pixel area, acquisition period, or sensor product; do not compute regional area or change.
N5｜no ground truth is provided; independent supporting data and a validation plan must be listed, and no classification accuracy may be declared.
Task and outputs
Recompute P1/P2 using NDVI=(NIR-RED)/(NIR+RED) and judge P3; make clear that quality screening precedes statistical interpretation.
Submit one page with the formulas, a valid/excluded/no-value table, and validation to-dos; make no real surface determination for fictional pixels.
Reference answer (complete it independently first)
P2 can be computed, but is excluded because the premise marks it cloud-contaminated; P3 has a denominator of 0, so NDVI is undefined. Only P1 can enter the valid table of this paper exercise.
N4/N5 lacks scale, time, real sensors, and independent ground truth, so regional area, surface class, change, or accuracy cannot be inferred.
Boundaries and review

NASA provides the NDVI concept; the quality flags in this exercise are editorial fiction, not Landsat bit encodings. Real product scaling, masking, registration, and validation follow the corresponding documentation; do not collect real sensitive locations.

subject.summary: Remote sensing scientists and technologists combine satellite, aerial, or ground sensor data with other geographic information, design analysis methods, validate results, and interpret resource, environmental, or urban problems. This page corresponds to O*NET 19-2099.01; public wage and employment statistics only go up to the broad 19-2099 category.
